events.title: Elizabeth Blackwell Becomes First Woman to Earn a Medical Degree in the U.S.
events.description: Elizabeth Blackwell graduated from Geneva Medical College in New York, becoming the first woman in the United States to receive a medical degree. She had been admitted, reportedly, after the student body voted in favor of her admission.
events.significance: Her achievement broke a major gender barrier in the medical profession and paved the way for women to enter medicine, inspiring later generations of female physicians.

events.title: Netherlands Refuses to Extradite Kaiser Wilhelm II
events.description: The Dutch government formally refused an Allied request to hand over former German Emperor Wilhelm II, who had fled to the Netherlands after World War I, to face trial for war crimes.
events.significance: The refusal meant the Kaiser never faced trial, shaping debates over accountability for wartime leaders and the limits of the Treaty of Versailles.

events.title: Twentieth Amendment Ratified
events.description: The Twentieth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified when Missouri became the 36th state to approve it. It moved the start of presidential terms from March 4 to January 20 and congressional terms to January 3.
events.significance: It shortened the 'lame duck' period between elections and inauguration, making transitions of power more prompt.

events.title: Bathyscaphe Trieste Reaches the Bottom of the Challenger Deep
events.description: Jacques Piccard and U.S. Navy Lieutenant Don Walsh descended in the bathyscaphe Trieste to the bottom of the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, about 10,900 meters (35,800 feet) below the surface.
events.significance: It was the first crewed descent to the deepest known point in the Earth's oceans, a landmark of deep-sea exploration.

events.title: Nixon Announces Vietnam Peace Agreement
events.description: President Richard Nixon announced that an agreement had been reached to end the Vietnam War, with the Paris Peace Accords initialed in Paris by Henry Kissinger and Le Duc Tho.
events.significance: The accords led to the withdrawal of U.S. combat forces from Vietnam, ending direct American involvement in the long and divisive conflict.
